notesDetails.title: Zero manage_task Polling Overhead: 0 Polls Across 11 Backgrounded Commands via Pure Reactive system_message Waiting
bullets: 0 `manage_task` Calls Across 344 Steps: Whenever a `run_command` exceeded the 10-second synchronous wait cap (`WaitMsBeforeAsync: 10000`), Antigravity CLI moved the task to the background (`11` times total: `task-60`, `task-75`, `task-193`, `task-205`, `task-239`, `task-269`, `task-290`, `task-295`, `task-303`, `task-330`, and `task-340`). On every single backgrounded command, `gemini-4-argon` output a one-line status update, ended its turn, and waited for the reactive `system_message` completion wakeup—making **`0` `manage_task` calls** across the entire run (compared to `7` on `gemini-4-carbon` and `105` on `gemini-3.8-flash-high`).

Aggressive Multi-Tool Batching (`1.53` Tools/Turn, 59 Multi-Tool Turns): Out of `131` LLM turns, `59` turns (`45.0%`) dispatched multiple parallel tool calls in a single response (up to `5` tools/turn, totaling `200` tool calls: `102` `run_command`, `67` `edit_file`, `19` `write_file`, `12` `read_file`).

Harness Comparison (`antigravity cli` vs. `omp` on `gemini-4-argon` High): Compared to `omp` running the same `gemini-4-argon` (`High`) model (`132` turns, `18.29M` tokens, `$3.97`, `53m`), `antigravity cli` matched the turn count almost identically (`131` vs. `132` turns) and cut total tokens by **`30.3%`** (`12.75M` vs. `18.29M`) and billed cost by **`15.1%`** (`$3.37` vs. `$3.97`) because its average prompt context stayed `24.6%` smaller (`96,277` vs. `127,667` tokens, peaking at `203,770` vs. `214,321`).

notesDetails.title: SIGTERM + +Bi Escript Wrapper Passed All Post-Boot PTY Ctrl-C Probes While Leaving a ~250 ms Early-Boot SIGTERM Race
bullets: Diagnosing `SIGUSR1` Crash Dumps & Choosing `SIGTERM` in `S1` (Steps `30–78`): During `S1`, the agent probed `:os.set_signal/2` on OTP 28 and observed that `SIGUSR1` triggered ERTS's default `Received SIGUSR1 / Crash dump is being written to: erl_crash.dump` handler (Step `43`) before custom handlers were swapped in. It therefore configured `mix.exs` with `escript: [main_module: CapyBench.CLI, path: "cb.escript", emu_args: "+Bi -noinput"]` and wrote `./cb` to trap `INT TERM`, forward `kill -TERM "$child"`, and loop `wait "$child"` until the child PID exits while `CapyBench.SignalHandler` swaps `:erl_signal_handler` on `:erl_signal_server` for `:sigterm`.

Holdout PTY `Ctrl-C` Audit (Post-Boot Pass vs. `20 ms–250 ms` Boot-Window Race): Against both local HTTP servers (`10 ms` fast pacing, `800 ms` slow in-flight, `3,000 ms` stalled in-flight) and live HTTPS (`https://rizafahmi.com`), sending `\x03` on a foreground PTY at `>= 350 ms` (`0.35s`, `0.40s`, `0.50s`, `0.55s`, `0.80s`) passed 100%—stopping new dispatches, printing a valid 6-line partial summary to `stdout` (`started == responses + failures`), emitting empty `stderr`, and exiting `130`. However, because `./cb` forwards `kill -TERM "$child"` immediately without a readiness handshake (`CB_READY_FILE`) or boot-time `SIG_IGN`, a `Ctrl-C` arriving during the first `~250 ms` of BEAM startup kills or interrupts the VM before `CapyBench.CLI.run_benchmark/2` calls `CapyBench.SignalHandler.install/1` (`20–50 ms` exits `143` via default `SIGTERM`; `100–250 ms` hits `{noproc, {gen_server, call, [elixir_config, ...]}}` or `:standard_io` EIO).

notesDetails.title: 53% Lower Cost Than gemini-4-carbon ($3.37 vs. $7.16), 96.75% Cache Hit Rate ($23.18 Saved) & 100% File-Edit Precision (86/86)
bullets: 100% File-Edit Success & Decomposition of the 27 Non-Zero `run_command` Exits: Every single `edit_file` (`67/67`), `write_file` (`19/19`), and `read_file` (`12/12`) call succeeded on the first try (`0` file-tool errors). All `27` tool errors were non-zero `run_command` exits: `16` deliberate red-phase TDD `mix test` runs confirming new tests failed before writing implementation code (`S1` Step `21`; `S2` Steps `96`, `102`, `108`, `114`, `120`, `126`; `S3` Steps `160`, `170`, `183`; `S4` Steps `214`, `220`, `228`; `S5` Step `249`; `S6` Step `281`; `S7` Step `312`), `4` `mix credo --strict` readability/nesting catches (`S3` Step `202`, `S4` Step `236`, `S5` Step `266`, `S7` Step `327`), `4` disposable OTP/PTY/PKI one-liners (`Steps 43, 60, 142, 151`), `2` intermediate S6 TLS test timing adjustments (`Steps 290, 295`), and `1` S7 unused-variable `--warnings-as-errors` catch (`Step 320`).

Unit Economics & Single Post-Turn-1 Cache Miss (`96.75%` Cache Hit Rate): Across `131` turns, `gemini-4-argon` processed `12,612,272` prompt tokens (`410,463` uncached at `$2.00/1M` = `$0.8209` + `12,201,809` cached at `$0.10/1M` = `$1.2202`) and `133,296` output tokens (including `52,223` thinking tokens) at `$10.00/1M` (`$1.3330`), totaling `12,745,568` tokens and `$3.3741` (`$3.37` under 2026 rates; `$6.75` under 2027 rates; saving `$23.18` / `87.3%` via prefix caching). Only one turn after Turn 1 experienced `cache_read_tokens: 0` (Step `38` during `S1` at `28,650` tokens), and even after Step `145`'s `3m 15s` API timeout, Step `146` resumed with a `68,907`-token cache hit.

Model Ablation on Antigravity CLI (`gemini-4-argon` vs. `gemini-4-carbon` High): Running on the exact same `antigravity cli` harness and `$2.00/$0.10/$10.00` rate card, `gemini-4-argon` finished `27m` faster (`61m` vs. `88m` active), used `33.8%` fewer LLM turns (`131` vs. `198`), `52.6%` fewer total tokens (`12.75M` vs. `26.88M`), and cut total cost by **`52.9%`** (`$3.37` vs. `$7.16`).
